text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester United and Everton at Old Trafford.

United manager Erik ten Hag is under increased pressure after back-to-back defeats in the Premier League have seen his side slip 11 points behind fourth-placed Aston Villa and a guaranteed place in next season's Champions League.
The Red Devils had strung four consecutive top-flight wins together in February to put them in a strong position, but defeats to Fulham and Manchester City have seen them drop to sixth place.
United looked like they were on for a shock victory in the derby when Marcus Rashford gave them the lead with a thunderous strike heading into half-time.
However, a brace from Phil Foden and a goal from Erling Haaland gave the Citizens a deserved victory, beating them 3.33-0.25 on xG (expected goals).
As Aston Villa and Tottenham play against each other tomorrow, one of United's rivals for a Champions League spot will certainly drop points, but it will only matter if the hosts win today.

Everton were handed a boost before their last Premier League outing against West Ham, with their appeal to reduce their 10-point punishment for breaching Profit and Sustainability Rules to six points lifting them from 17th to 15th.
As a result, the Toffees moved five points clear of the relegation zone.
However, their disappointing run in the top-flight continued, with the Hammers' stoppage-time victory extending Everton's winless run to 10 games.

They also had the lead at half-time after Beto made up for his penalty miss by scoring a header, but goals from Kurt Zouma, Tomas Soucek and Edson Alvarez helped David Moyes' men to all three points at Goodison Park.
There is another possible points deduction for Everton looming, so an upturn in results is desperately needed for Sean Dyche to push them well away from the drop zone.
United select the same side that started their 3-1 defeat to rivals City in their previous Premier League outing.
Evans and Rashford were forced off with injuries against the Citizens but are fit enough to keep their place in the team.
Youngsters Collyer and Ogunneye are on the bench and could make their top-flight debut for the Red Devils.
Dyche also keeps the faith in his side that were beaten 3-1 by West Ham in their last match.
There was a chance that Idrissa Gueye could’ve been fit enough to feature, but he hasn’t recovered from a groin injury and is out of the squad.

United have won all three of their Premier League games against Everton since the start of last season, while they last won four league meetings in a row against the Toffees from November 2006 to December 2007.
Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
United get this Premier League clash under way.
Fernandes has the first kick.
Both teams desperately need a win.
United are put under pressure by Everton's early pressure in their defensive third, but Beto's low cross is blocked.
The ball bobbles around the box, and neither side can take control, but the Red Devils eventually win it back.
McNeil wins an early corner on the left, with Garner strolling over to take it.
However, his inswinging cross is headed away by Evans.
McNeil swings a deep cross from the left into the box, with Amadou Onana attacking it.
The ball drops to Godfrey, who attempts to flick a shot at goal, but Andre Onana rushes off his line bravely to smother it.
Fernandes collects possession in the middle of Everton's half and offloads a pass to Garnacho on his right.
He strides forward and rolls the ball into Dalot, but he takes a heavy touch inside the box, allowing Onana to clear it well away.
Everton are looking sharp, but it could be that United are also gifting them the ball too often.
Beto slides a pass out to Doucoure on the right, but his cross is claimed by Onana, who dives across the box.
CHANCE! United go close out of nothing! Fernandes has the ball in United's half and switches the play over to Rashford, who darts down the left and into space.
He gets past Mykolenko to get a shot away, but Harrison does brilliantly to get back and make an important block.
Fernandes takes the following corner from the right, swinging the ball onto Casemiro's header.
However, his flicked effort is easily saved by Pickford.
PENALTY UNITED! The hosts have a chance to take the lead from the spot! Rashford comes down the left and slides a pass into Garnacho, who flicks the ball past Tarkowski and is tripped inside the box.
There is a VAR check for offside, but the penalty stands!
GOALLLL! FERNANDES SCORES! 1-0 UNITED! What a penalty from Fernandes! The captain is cool under pressure, curling his penalty into the bottom-right corner.
Pickford goes the right way, but he is beaten by the accuracy of the strike.
CHANCE! Everton almost responded immediately.
The ball drops kindly to McNeil on the box, with the winger volleying a left-footed effort just wide of the left post.
Onana could only stand and watch the ball go just wide.
There is a loud atmosphere at Old Trafford, which could be inspired by the recent news that new co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe wants to build a new stadium.
There has been some backlash, but all the home fans will set aside their concerns today and focus on supporting their side, looking to help United avoid defeat for the first time in three matches.
Fernandes' goal came at the right time, with Everton building in confidence after a bright start.
Branthwaite has possession in Everton's half and looks to roll a throughball behind United's defence and into Beto, but the flag goes up for offside immediately.
The striker was quite far off, as the play wasn't even allowed to continue to its conclusion.
Varane comes forward down the left and switches a pass over to Garnacho on the right.
He is in space and cuts the ball into Fernandes in the middle of the box, but he scoops his first-time strike well over.
United regain possession on the halfway line, with McTominay ignoring Garnacho on the right and instead looking for Rashford on the left.
However, he puts too much power on the ball, allowing Pickford to run off his line to claim it just inside the box.
Everton are getting shots away, but they are all coming from outside the box.
This time, Harrison is given the time and space to crash a left-footed effort towards the goal, with his strike going well over the bar.
Beto wrestles for the ball against Evans on the halfway line, throwing his arm in the face of the centre-back.
Everton's attack comes to nothing, but Evans isn’t happy with the striker.
However, VAR sees no wrongdoing from the Portuguese forward.
Godfrey gets to the byline and flashes a cross into the box, but it goes just past Beto in the middle.
Everton retain possession through McNeil, who looks for another cross.
However, Varane shields it behind.
United gift the ball back to Everton again, but Mykolenko's strike from the edge is quickly blocked behind by Casemiro.
Garner lifts his right-footed cross towards the back post, but Tarkowski cannot turn his header on target.
CHANCE! Another opportunity for Everton.
Garner has space around him after playing a clever one-two outside United's box, but his strike is pushed away by Andre Onana.
The goalkeeper pushes it straight out to Amadou Onana, who takes a touch before blasting his attempt well over.
Amadou Onana is the first player to be shown a yellow card after fouling Garnacho on the edge of the Everton box.
SAVE! Fernandes is denied his second goal.
The captain takes responsibility for a free-kick just to the left outside the box and whips his right-footed effort towards the top-left corner.
However, Pickford gets across his line to push it away at full stretch.
CHANCE! Wonderful play from United.
Rashford has possession on the left and switches the play over to Fernandes on the right side of the box.
He rolls it through to McTominay, who thumps a cutback towards Mainoo.
However, Branthwaite slides it away before the flag goes up for offside.
Evans concedes possession in United's half to Beto, allowing Everton to commit men forward on the attack.
McNeil receives it on the left on the edge of the box and drives a low strike just wide of the right post.
Everton are winless in 10 Premier League games (drawing five and losing five), the longest ongoing run of any side currently in the division.
Only from August to October 1994 (12) have the Toffees ever had a longer winless run in the competition.
PENALTY UNITED! The hosts have the chance to double their lead after some superb work from Garnacho again.
The Argentine drives from right to left on the edge of the box before being clattered by Godfrey.
Two clumsy moments have cost Everton, who have been threatening on the attack.
Doucoure is not happy with the penalty being given and is shown a yellow card.
GOALLLL! RASHFORD SCORES! 2-0 UNITED! Fernandes scored the last penalty but gives this one to Rashford.
The England international stutters on his run towards the ball before driving his strike into the bottom-left corner.
Pickford commits himself the other way.
Garnacho is the first player to win two penalties in a single Premier League game since Antonio Rudiger for Chelsea v Leeds in December 2021, and the first ever to do so for United.
Everton win a free-kick just inside United's half.
Pickford launches the ball forward, but Casemiro gets up head it away from danger just inside the box.

Everton have the 10th-highest xG in the Premier League this season (42.5), but the third-lowest goal total (29), giving them the biggest difference between expected goals and goals scored in the competition this term (13.5).
The Toffees have created an xG of 0.9 against United, but have only hit the target twice with their nine shots.
Fernandes has possession in United's box, but he sends a pass straight to McNeil.
The ball then rolls to Godfrey, who drives a low shot from the edge towards the bottom-left corner, but it deflects off Evans and goes behind.
Godfrey is well up the pitch, so when Everton concede possession, it gives Fernandes the chance to dash into the space left behind by the right-back.
He gets into the box and attempts to curl a pass into the middle with the outside of his foot, but the ball is blocked, and Pickford comes out to claim it.
PENALTY SHOUT! United want a third penalty.
Garnacho rushes down the right and gets to the byline before cutting the ball back across the box.
Mykolenko slides to the floor, and the ball hits his supporting hand, but no penalty is given.
Ten Hag is furious.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Mainoo and McTominay combine down the left side of the box, but the ball gets trapped under the feet of the Scotland international.
He rolls a pass back to Casemiro on the edge of the box, with the midfielder's low, first-time strike blocked by Onana.
Garnacho has been United's best player.
He breaks forward on the right and drives into the box, faking it shoot to put Branthwaite on the floor before the centre-back gets across to recover.
He had options in the middle, but nobody was complaining after his first-half performance.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-0 EVERTON
United scored two penalties in the first half to lead a wasteful Everton 2-0 heading into half-time at Old Trafford.
Garnacho was the Red Devils' star, winning both spot-kicks to give the hosts a comfortable advantage.
He was first tripped by Tarkowski, allowing captain Fernandes to curl his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner.
Harrison and Garner tested Onana, but it was Ten Hag's men that scored again.
Garnacho was tricky on the edge of the box, driving across from right to left before being bundled to the floor by Godfrey.
Rashford took the penalty this time, stuttering with his run towards the ball before directing his shot into the bottom-left corner.
It looks like United deserve their lead by a distance at half-time after creating an xG of 2.02, but the statistics have been heavily inflated by the two penalties.
Despite not getting an assist to his name, Garnacho has been their best player, constantly driving at the Everton defence and winning two penalties.
As for Everton, it's more of the same.
Dyche was getting frustrated in the dugout, and there should be no surprise with his side failing to convert their opportunities again.
The away side have registered an xG of 1.07 from their 11 shots but have only hit the target twice.
They have had 29 final third entries and 17 touches inside the opposition box but nothing to show for it.
Everton get the ball rolling again.
They need an early goal in the second half if they want to get back into the contest.
The Toffees are on their way to an 11th consecutive Premier League game without a win.
United have won 180 and lost none of the 185 previous occasions they have been two or more goals ahead at half-time in the Premier League (drawing five).
Meanwhile, away from home, Everton have lost 54 and won none of the 57 previous times they have been two or more goals behind at the break in the competition (drawing three).
Not an encouraging statistic if you’re an Everton fan or Dyche.
The Toffees have had most of the possession since the restart and are trying to build an attack.
Harrison collects the ball in the middle of United's half and spreads a pass down the right to Godfrey, who sends his cross behind for a goal-kick.
Young or Coleman are better going forward than the former Norwich City man, but they are on the bench.
CHANCE! Everton go short with a free-kick on the left, unleashing McNeil on the wing.
His inswinging cross is headed into the path of Doucoure by Tarkowski, but his strike in the middle of the box is blocked by McTominay.
Doucoure is Everton’s top scorer in the Premier League with six goals this season, though he hasn’t scored since December.

Since Dyche became manager of the club last February, the Toffees have won 36 per cent of their league games when Doucoure starts (13/36), winning none of their nine when he doesn’t (drawing three and losing six).
OVER! Garnacho goes close! Fernandes spins in possession in the heart of Everton's half and rolls a pass out to Garnacho, who drives into the box.
He is put under pressure by Mykolenko and lifts his right-footed strike over the bar.
Everton try to build an attack around the halfway line, but Onana puts too much power on his first-time pass, sending the ball out for a goal-kick.
The Toffees are getting some substitutes ready to come on.
Beto has his first shot inside United's box, but his attempt is blocked.
The ball spins up in the air, with the forward heading a pass down to Doucoure.
The midfielder drives a low strike towards the near post, but Onana stops it with his feet.
WIDE! McTominay battles with Garner inside United's half, pushing him away before slotting a pass down the left to Fernandes.
He gets into Everton's defensive third and sends an inviting cross towards Garnacho, but he pokes his effort wide on the slide.
Dyche has seen enough and has decided to make three changes.
Beto has had 24 touches and one shot up front for Everton and is being replaced by Calvert-Lewin.
The Englishman has scored three goals in 23 appearances.
Harrison also makes his way off the pitch at the nearest side.
Dobbin is on, with his only Premier League goal coming against Chelsea in a 2-0 win earlier in the season.
There is also a straight swap in the midfield.
Doucoure is replaced by Gomes.
SAVE! Brave from Pickford! Fernandes' inswinging cross from the right bobbles around the middle of the box, with Lindelof poking his shot towards the goal.
Pickford claims it under pressure from Evans, who catches the goalkeeper and apologises immediately.
Gomes has space outside United's box and rolls a pass down the right to Dobbin for his first involvement.
He takes a heavy touch but still finds a way to win a corner off Lindelof.
Lindelof barges into the back of Onana trying to win possession and gives away a poor free-kick in shooting range for Everton.
The experienced Gomes takes aim from range, but his right-footed strike is blocked by the wall.
OVER! Dobbin gets a shot away, but it’s poor.
Calvert-Lewin wrestles for the ball on the edge of the box but cannot turn away from his marker and rolls the ball back to Dobbin, who lashes a first-time strike with his left foot high and wide.
McTominay crashes into the back of Onana and is shown a yellow card.
He was desperate to win possession in Everton's half, but he was clumsy.
United’s 40 Premier League wins against Everton is the joint-most one side has against another in the competition’s history, with the Red Devils also winning 40 times against Villa.
They have only had four shots in the second half compared to Everton's seven, but they look comfortable.
However, a shock goal from the Toffees could put them under pressure.
Nothing seems to be happening for Calvert-Lewin.
He is working hard up front and puts pressure on Varane, but his back to Onana just about has enough weight on it for the goalkeeper to get there and clear.
The Toffees get it back through McNeil.
However, his cross goes straight to the goalkeeper.
There is a light round of applause from the home fans around the dugout as Young steps away from the bench to come on.
He replaces Garner, who also spent time at the Red Devils.
WIDE! How have Everton not scored? Mykolenko flashes a brilliant cross from the left over to Godfrey, who heads the ball back across the goal.
Dobbin is there, but his shot from a narrow angle goes back across Andre Onana and wide.
He might have been looking for Calvert-Lewin, who was looking the other way.
Amadou Onana goes for an ambitious overhead kick from outside the box, but his shot is saved with ease by Andre Onana.
That would have been goal of the season if it went in, but it never looked likely.
United make their first change.
Mainoo was comfortable in the midfield and won three of his duels, but is now coming off for Amrabat.
Everton have had twice as many shots in the second half than United (8-4), also having more touches in the box (16-11).
However, they have only created an xG of 0.41 since the restart and have had too many nearly moments.
McNeil floats a corner from the right onto Calvert-Lewin, but he cannot get enough power on his header, with the ball going straight into Onana's gloves.
Garnacho is denied the chance of an unlikely hat-trick of penalty wins, but he will be delighted with his contributions, turning the contest in United's favour with his direct runs into the box.
He is off for Antony, who still has a lot to prove.
Young gets down the right and whips a corner towards the back post, with Mykolenko getting forward.
Antony gets back well to defend it, forcing the left-back to direct his header wide.
United's work was done in the first half with the two penalties that they scored, but their performance since the restart has been pretty flat.
They have only registered an xG of 0.54, hitting the target with two of their four shots.
If Everton weren’t so clumsy in their box, the Red Devils would be playing in a much closer contest.
Chermiti comes on for his 11th Premier League appearance for Everton, still waiting for his first goal.
Mykolenko is off, in what is a very late attacking change from Dyche, who probably should’ve done it a lot earlier.
United switch experience for youth in the defence.
Evans is off for Kambwala, who makes his fourth Premier League appearance at centre-back for the hosts.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Antony surges down the left and wins a late corner off Branthwaite.
Fernandes elects to take it short, and the hosts work it out to Dalot outside the box, but he curls his right-footed strike straight at Pickford.
It's interesting that United are two goals ahead and have only made three changes, but Diallo hasn’t been given an opportunity off the bench.
He has plenty of potential but only made two Premier League appearances this season.
OFFSIDE! Fernandes skips past a couple of tackles and slides a pass through to Rashford.
He gets into the box and skips past Branthwaite, who takes down the forward.
The referee blows for a penalty before changing his arm movement for an offside call.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-0 EVERTON
Fernandes and Rashford scored first-half penalties for United to help the Red Devils beat Everton 2-0 at Old Trafford.
It was more frustration for Dyche, who watched his team extend their run to 11 games without a win in the Premier League despite creating an xG of 1.48.
Ten Hag's men made the most of their wasteful attacking and clumsy tackles, with Garnacho winning two penalties.
First tripped by Tarkowski, captain Fernandes took responsibility from the spot and curled his shot into the bottom-right corner.
Godfrey was the next player to barge into Garnacho inside the box after a tricky run from the Argentine.
Rashford drilled his shot into the opposite corner, with United becoming just the third team in Premier League history to have two different players score a penalty in the first half.

events.action: drilled his shot into the opposite corner

text: Everton had 12 attempts in the second half but couldn’t make any of their chances count.
Dobbin had their best opportunity, but he flashed his effort across goal and away from danger.
Next, United host Liverpool in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup.
As for Everton, they go to Bournemouth in the Premier League in three weeks.
That's all for today, goodbye.
